## Idea
Kahn ordering uses the heap ready set; CPM computes earliest/latest times, slack and one deterministic critical path for a DAG with non-negative integer durations.

## Complexity
O((V+E) log V) ready-frontier work plus graph/time passes, expected constant-time hashing; O(V+E) storage. Cycle reporting additionally computes SCCs.

## Use when
Schedule precedence constraints or explain the duration-determining path.

## Avoid when
Resources or temporal uncertainty constrain the schedule: CPM alone does not solve resource scheduling.

## Pitfalls
The order must be a total preorder for its specified least-first tie contract. Negative durations/overflow refuse; cycle Error must be handled. Makespan is not a probabilistic forecast.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph.TopoSort.sort: ('N -> 'N -> int) -> 'N list -> ('N -> 'N list) -> Result<'N list,'N list list> when 'N: equality`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph
let next n = if n = 1 then [2] else []
let order = TopoSort.sort compare [1; 2] next
let schedule = TopoSort.criticalPath compare [1; 2] next (fun _ -> 3)
```

## Tests
TopoSortTests: list-model total/non-total orders, SCC cycle oracle, brute-force longest path and CPM identities, equally critical predecessors and 100000-node chain.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains graph/topological-sort-cpm/random-dag. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
